claims.summary: (1) For N-point sets X,Y in [0,1]^2, a grid of square cells of side delta, cell-uniform smearings mu_X, mu_Y, a bijection pi with D_i the difference of the centres of the cells of Y_pi(i) and X_i, tube density rho_pi(x) = delta^(-2) sum_i Leb{t in [0,1]: x - t D_i in Q(X_i)}, convex phi_j with phi_j(0)=0 and conjugates phi_j*, every Lipschitz G and lambda>0: int G d(mu_X - mu_Y) <= lambda sum_j [sum_i phi_j(|D_i^j|/lambda) + int phi_j*(|d_j G|) rho_pi dx]. (2) With alpha_j in [1,infinity], phi_j = psi_alpha_j, delta <= s, sum_i psi_alpha_j(|X_i^j - Y^j_pi(i)|/s) <= N for j=1,2 and rho_pi <= K N: every Lipschitz G with int sum_j psi*_alpha_j(|d_j G|) <= 2 has int G d(mu_X - mu_Y) <= 2(e+2K) s N.
claims.assessment: Working proof: translation of each cell's uniform mass to its partner cell, the fundamental theorem of calculus along the swept cells (Rademacher, Fubini) and the Fenchel-Young inequality coordinatewise; part (2) with lambda = 2s, convexity and psi_alpha(1) <= e-1. Deterministic. A converse of the Hopf-Lax reduction up to constants and grid, conditional on a matching of bounded tube density; the registered normalization of the class bound (factor 1/2, grid s/32) is not matched.
claims.rationale: Gives a sufficient condition for the converse of the Hopf-Lax reduction: the conjecture plus one good matching of tube density O(N) implies the class bound up to constants and grid, which implies the conjecture; bounded density is not shown necessary.
claims.next_action: Test the tube-density condition against the Leighton-Shor sets: count the crossings a good matching must carry and the long pairs the exponential condition allows.

relationships: The converse direction of that reduction, up to constants and grid, for matchings of bounded tube density.
The forward Fenchel-Young bound from a flow; this one bounds the class from a matching's swept cells.
Up to constants and grid, the class bound follows from the conjecture whenever a good matching of tube density O(N) exists.
